sections.h2: Fastest ways to sell in Bridgewater Township
sections.html:
An owner in a hurry can accept a cash offer, hire a listing agent, or find a buyer without one. In this township the listing route is strong, because prices are high and buyers are plentiful, so people pick cash for other reasons: a house in need of work, a relocation date, an estate, or a landlord leaving the business.

Bridgewater sits in the middle of Somerset County, about 32 miles from Manhattan, and has 46,455 residents.

Bridgewater is among the pricier towns in central New Jersey. The median owner-occupied value is $605,500, 84.9% of homes are owner-occupied, median household income is $172,851 and median gross rent is $2,176. Median owner costs with a mortgage run $3,258 a month, so buyers are sensitive to taxes and condition.

The township mixes older neighborhoods with large newer developments. Buyers talk about it in sections that have no formal borders:

  • Bradley Gardens, an older southwestern area with newer pockets and a commercial strip on Old York Road.
  • Green Knoll, the central area with Bridgewater Commons, the municipal building and the high school.
  • Finderne, in the southeast, with older streets and newer developments.
  • Martinsville, the largest census-designated place, and Bridgewater Center in the west.

Average travel time to work is 31.4 minutes. Interstate 287 is the main limited-access road, Interstate 78 passes through the north without exits, and U.S. 22, Route 28 and Routes 202-206 cross the township. The Raritan Valley Line stops at Bridgewater station, and NJ Transit buses run to the Port Authority Bus Terminal (route 114) and Newark (route 65). Newark Liberty Airport is about 25 miles away.

Buyers moving from New York or north Jersey often ask which streets are closest to the station and the highways, so put that in the listing.

Most of the township is in the Bridgewater-Raritan Regional School District, which also serves the borough of Raritan. Primary schools feed intermediate schools for grades 5 and 6, then a middle school for grades 7 and 8 and a high school for grades 9 through 12. Because buyers often shop by elementary zone, confirm the primary school for your street with the district before you advertise it.

sections.h2: Permits before you renovate or sell
sections.html:
Code Enforcement administers construction permits and issues certificates of approval and occupancy after final inspection. A permit is generally needed for decks, pools, additions, garages, finishing a basement, new electrical outlets, and new or replacement furnaces, water heaters or air conditioning. A shed needs one if it is over 200 square feet or has utilities, a fence only if it is over 6 feet or serves as a pool barrier, and roofing only where sheathing is replaced. State law lets the construction official fine unpermitted work up to $2,000 per violation, which is why open or missing permits surface during a buyer's review. Plan review can take up to 20 working days.

Home fire safety requirements and applications are handled by the Fire Safety office. Call the main line at 908-725-6300, extension 5560 for construction questions and extension 5550 for fire safety, to confirm what a buyer's inspection will check. The municipal offices are at 100 Commons Way.

Bridgewater bills in four installments, with a ten-day grace period. If the lender escrows your taxes, the lender must supply the correct bank code to the tax office, and when a mortgage is paid off at closing the office should be told to remove it. The assessor runs an annual reassessment program, and each property is inspected on a four-year cycle, so a visit from the township's appraisal contractor before a sale is not unusual.

sections.h2: State fees on a higher-priced sale
sections.html:
With a median value above $600,000, many Bridgewater sales exceed the thresholds in New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee schedule. The seller pays at recording. For deals above $350,000 the rate per $500 of price runs $2.90 on the first $150,000, $4.25 up to $200,000, $4.80 up to $550,000 and $5.30 from $550,000 to $850,000.

When the price tops $1,000,000 for a residential property, a supplemental Graduated Percent Fee applies, and the seller owes it. The band starts at 1% for sales up to $2,000,000 and climbs in steps to 3.5% on the very top prices. Exemption forms, including RTF-1EE, are posted by the Division of Taxation. Compare a cash buyer's lower price against these fees plus commission, not just the headline number.

The Raritan River forms much of the southern edge, and the North Branch of the Raritan marks the western border. If your home is low-lying near the river, ask the township engineering office about flood information before you list, and keep any flood insurance and repair records for the buyer. The northeastern part, by contrast, is hilly because the First Watchung Mountain runs through it.

After you sign a contract, ask Code Enforcement to confirm that every permit has a final inspection, and call Fire Safety to learn what the buyer's inspection will check. Ask the Tax Collector for the current quarter's balance and tell the office when a mortgage will be paid off at closing. Your attorney orders the title work, the deed goes to the county for recording and the seller's transfer fee is paid at that point. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, but these township and state steps still apply, so start them in the first week.

Keep a folder with your deed, permit records for the deck, basement or any addition, the last two tax bills and any flood or repair paperwork. Buyers in this price range ask for documents early, and a complete folder shortens the back and forth. If you plan to move before closing, tell your attorney so keys, utility transfers and the final walk-through are scheduled around your date. On the closing day you sign the deed and the seller's tax forms, the lender is paid off, and the proceeds are wired to you once the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When are Bridgewater property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, each with a ten-day grace period. A tenth day that lands on a weekend or holiday moves the cutoff to the next business day.

faqs.q: When must a Bridgewater assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: May 1 of the tax year. Confirm the date against the notice you receive from the Tax Assessor at 908-725-6300, extension 5121.

faqs.q: Does a Bridgewater shed or fence need a permit?
faqs.a: Only in some cases. A shed needs a permit if it is over 200 square feet or has electric or plumbing, and a fence needs one if it is over 6 feet tall or serves as a pool barrier.
The Bridgewater-Raritan Regional School District, which covers pre-kindergarten through grade 12 for Bridgewater and the borough of Raritan.

faqs.q: Does a sale above $1,000,000 cost more in New Jersey?
faqs.a: Yes. Residential sales above $1,000,000 carry a Graduated Percent Fee on top of the Realty Transfer Fee, starting at 1% of total consideration, and the seller is responsible for it.
